name: Python
summary: Dynamically typed, garbage-collected general-purpose language with indentation-based block structure, a large standard library and optional (gradual) type annotations; defined by the Python Language Reference and the PEP process, with CPython as the reference implementation.

level_notes.0: CPython (C) is the reference implementation: PEG grammar in Grammar/python.gram, compiler and bytecode interpreter in Python/, built-in types in Objects/; its InternalDocs/ directory documents the internals. PyPy (RPython, meta-tracing JIT), MicroPython, GraalPy, Jython, IronPython and RustPython are independent implementations.
level_notes.1: No ISO/ECMA standard. The Python Language Reference and Library Reference (docs.python.org) are normative together with accepted PEPs; the static type system has its own specification at typing.python.org. Where the reference is silent, CPython behaviour is the de facto definition.
level_notes.2: The official Tutorial and HOWTOs are level 2; there is no HOPL paper, so Guido van Rossum's 'History of Python' blog and the Design and History FAQ serve as history sources.
level_notes.3: Rosetta Code reports 'blocked' to automated checkers from the research sandbox.
